text:
Piece Puzzle · 4-player individual match

1. Objective
Each player uses the same eight Pieces in five types to complete a grid of four rows crossing four columns.
Compete for your own survival. The first 3 players to submit a completed puzzle survive, and the last 1 is eliminated for good.
Each player works on their own board in private, without conversation, negotiation, or relationship reviews.

2. Notches and orientation
Each Piece has 4 notches. side 0 is a notch cut from the top, and side 1 is a notch cut from the bottom.
depth is the notch depth when the Piece height is taken as 100, and is one of 33, 58, or 83.
The two notches at each crossing must face opposite sides, top and bottom, and their depths must sum to at least 100.
Read the notches on row Pieces from left to right, and on column Pieces from top to bottom.
reverse=true reverses the notch order, and flip=true swaps the top and bottom directions of every notch.

3. Gameplay
Each turn, everyone simultaneously and privately chooses one action: place, remove, submit with the buzzer, or pass.
When placing a Piece, specify a position from 1 to 4 in a horizontal row or vertical col. You may reposition a Piece already on the board.
If another Piece occupies the chosen slot, it returns to the tray. Only a placed Piece can be removed.
Specify the final position and orientation for the Piece. The notch conditions at the crossings determine whether it fits.
Even with all 8 Pieces placed and all 16 crossings fitting, you must press the buzzer with submit to submit a completed puzzle.
After an incorrect submission, you can adjust your board and submit again.

4. Rankings
Players who submit a completed puzzle on an earlier turn rank higher. Ties on the same turn are decided by the draw order announced at the start.
The game ends once three survivors are determined, and all final boards are revealed. You cannot see other players' boards during the game.
Once the model-call limit is reached, play continues with scripted default actions. Malformed model actions are treated as passes.

fields.note: P01 needs at least 8 placement actions and a buzzer submission, so placement begins on the first turn. K1 goes in the first row, and the remaining Pieces' orientations will be chosen to satisfy the crossing conditions.
P02 needs at least 8 placements and a buzzer submission, so starts placing Pieces immediately. Place K1 as the reference for the first row, then match the directions and depths of the column Pieces.
P16 needs at least eight placements and a buzzer submission, so placement begins immediately. Use K1 as the reference for the first row, then check the column Pieces' orientations and depths.

P03 needs at least 8 placements followed by the buzzer, so assembly begins immediately. K1 serves as the reference in the first row, and the directions and depths of the crossing notches will be checked as play continues.

P01 places K2 in row 2, aiming to submit on turn 9. The planned solution has K1, K2, and K3 in their original orientations and K5 reversed as the rows; the columns are K7 flipped, then K6, K8, and K4 in their original orientations, satisfying all 16 crossing conditions.

P02 matches K1's second notch (0/83) with the first notch of reversed K4 (1/33). The sides are opposite and the depths sum to 116, so the current crossing fits. Continue placing Pieces to finish in the fewest turns.

P16 confirmed that placing K4 in reverse in column 2 gives it the opposite direction to K1 and a depth sum of 116. The completion plan is rows K1, K2, and K3 in their original orientation and K5 in reverse; columns K6 with reverse and flip, K4 with reverse, K7 with reverse and flip, and K8 with reverse and flip. This satisfies all 16 crossing conditions.
P03 places a new Piece to finish in the minimum number of turns. Placing K6 in column 1 in its original orientation makes its crossing with K1 fit, with opposite directions and a depth sum of 141.

P01 has checked the orientations of the two existing rows and the remaining planned Pieces, confirming that all 16 crossing requirements can be met. Place K3 in row 3 in its original orientation to stay on track for the earliest possible turn 9 submission.

P02 confirmed a complete arrangement satisfying all 16 crossings while retaining the two existing placements. Placing K2 in its original orientation in the second row and then placing the remaining Pieces will allow a buzzer submission without further changes.

P16 confirms that the existing crossings have no errors, and that placing K2 in row 2 in its original orientation gives an opposite direction to K4 and a depth sum of 116. Continue the verified solution, aiming for the earliest submission.

P03 has confirmed that the existing crossings fit. Place K5 reversed in row 4, aiming to submit on turn 9. Then flipping K3 in row 2, flipping K2 in row 3, reversing K8 in column 2, placing K7 in its original orientation in column 3, and reversing and flipping K4 in column 4 can make all 16 crossings fit.
P01 checked that placing K5 in reverse in row 4 and K7 with a flip, K6, K8, and K4 in the columns satisfies all 16 crossing conditions. Placement continues toward a completed submission on turn 9.

P02 confirms that the two current crossings are valid. Placing K7 reversed and flipped in the third row allows a solution that preserves the existing arrangement, so proceed toward a turn-9 submission without spending turns on corrections.

P16 has confirmed that both current crossings are valid. Placing K3 in row 3 in its original orientation also fits K4, with opposite notch sides and a combined depth of 116. Aim for the earliest turn 9 submission without repositioning any Pieces.

P03 confirmed that placing K3 with a flip in row 2 gives it the opposite direction to K6 and a depth sum of 141. Adding a new Piece according to the verified complete arrangement keeps the earliest possible turn 9 submission on track.
P01 confirms that placing K7 flipped in column 1 gives opposite directions at all four crossings and depth sums of at least 100. Continue placing Pieces toward a completed submission on turn 9.

P02 has confirmed that all three current crossings fit. Placing K5 flipped in row 4 allows the remaining K6, K3, and K8 to fit columns 1, 3, and 4 respectively. Continue toward a turn 9 completed submission without revisions.

P16 confirmed that placing K5 in reverse in row 4 gives it the opposite direction to K4 and a depth sum of 166. Continuing the error-free arrangement preserves the possibility of submitting as early as turn 9.

P03 confirms that placing K2 flipped in row 3 gives an opposite direction to K6 in column 1 and a depth sum of 116. Continue the verified solution, aiming for the earliest possible buzzer submission on turn 9.

P01 has confirmed that placing K6 in column 2 in its original orientation gives opposite notch sides at all four crossings, with combined depths of at least 100. Continue placing without revisions, aiming for the earliest possible turn 9 completed submission.

P02 confirmed that placing K6 with reverse and flip in column 1 gives it the opposite direction to all four rows and depth sums of at least 100. Placing the remaining three Pieces without changes keeps the turn 9 submission path on track.

P16 confirms that placing K6 reversed and flipped in column 1 gives opposite directions against all four rows and depth sums of at least 116. Fill the remaining columns as planned, aiming for the earliest possible submission on turn 9.

P03 has confirmed that placing K8 reversed in column 2 gives opposite notch sides at all four crossings, with combined depths of at least 100. Fill the remaining columns in order to stay on track for the earliest turn 9 submission.

P01 confirmed that placing K8 in its original orientation in column 3 gives all four crossings opposite notch directions and depth sums of 141, 141, 116, and 116 respectively. The remaining placements will proceed toward a turn 9 submission.

P02 confirms that placing K3 in column 3 in its original orientation gives opposite directions and depth sums of at least 100 at all four crossings. Place the remaining K8, then proceed to the earliest possible submission on turn 9.

P16 has confirmed that all eight existing crossings are valid. Placing K7 reversed and flipped in column 3 gives opposite notch sides against all four rows, with combined depths of at least 100. Continue toward a turn 9 submission without repositioning any Pieces.

P03 confirmed that placing K7 in its original orientation in column 3 gives all four crossings opposite notch directions and depth sums of at least 100. Placing K7 now and K4 next prepares a buzzer submission on turn 9.

P01 confirms that placing the remaining K4 in column 4 in its original orientation gives opposite directions at the four crossings and depth sums of 166, 116, 116, and 116. Complete the arrangement this turn, then press the buzzer next turn to try to survive.

P02 has confirmed that placing K8 reversed and flipped in column 4 gives opposite notch sides at all four crossings, with combined depths of at least 100. Finish placement this turn and press the buzzer next turn to try to survive.

P16 confirmed that placing K8 with reverse and flip in column 4 gives it the opposite direction to all four rows and depth sums of 141, 141, 116, and 166 respectively. This placement completes all 16 crossings, preparing a buzzer submission next turn.

P03 confirms that placing K4 reversed and flipped in column 4 gives opposite directions at all four crossings and depth sums of 116, 116, 116, and 166, respectively. This placement completes the grid; prepare to submit with the buzzer next turn.
P01 has confirmed that all eight Pieces and all 16 crossings are correct. Press the buzzer immediately to secure the earliest completed submission and survival.

P02 confirmed that all 8 Pieces and 16 crossings are correct. Submitting immediately completes the puzzle on turn 9, the earliest possible turn. Being second in the draw order for simultaneous submissions also favors survival.

P16 confirms that all 8 Pieces and all 16 crossings are valid. Submitting immediately achieves the minimum completion time of 9 turns; even if everyone finishes simultaneously, they survive at rank 3 in the draw order.

P03 has confirmed that all eight Pieces and all 16 crossings are correct. The drawn order is unfavorable for same-turn submissions, but delaying would only lower the chance of survival, so press the buzzer immediately.
